With the 10-year yield above 5%, Treasuries offer a real alternative to stocks for cautious money.

items.headline: Health care deal Monday: Lilly buys Calytrix for up to $1.5B; Medtronic adds Contego
items.caption: Eli Lilly agreed to buy blood cancer biotech Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5 billion. Medtronic plans to buy Contego Medical, valued at $380 million.
detail: Eli Lilly is buying Calytrix Bio, a Massachusetts startup working on an antibody for two rare blood cancers, myelofibrosis and essential thrombocythemia. The deal is worth up to $1.5 billion, but the guaranteed cash portion wasn't disclosed. It extends Lilly's recent buying streak.

Medtronic plans to buy Contego Medical, which makes carotid artery and clot-removal devices. Medtronic already distributed Contego's products in the US. It expects a small hit to adjusted earnings per share in fiscal 2027 and 2028, then a neutral or positive effect.
money: 'Up to' deal prices include milestone payments that may never be paid, so the real cost is often lower.
Drug giants with big cash flow keep buying startups; health care funds give broad exposure without picking winners.
Small earnings dilution from deals is normal; watch whether the buyer delivers the promised growth later.
risk: Early-stage drugs often fail in trials.

money: Big product launches are often priced in early; shares can fall even on strong sales.
If you're buying the game, compare console bundles and retailer deals before launch day.
Gaming stocks swing on single titles, so a broad fund spreads that hit-or-miss risk.
risk: Delays or weak early sales could hit the stock hard.

detail: Unite union members at Apache's UK North Sea operations are striking again over jobs, pay and conditions. Apache offered a 4% raise, matching what non-union staff got. The union warns disruption at Forties Charlie could affect the Forties Pipeline System, which carries crude from more than 80 fields and about 29% of Britain's oil.
money: Supply hiccups in the North Sea can nudge Brent crude, which affects fuel prices far beyond the UK.
Energy funds can benefit from supply scares, but these moves often fade fast.
Labor disputes are a real cost for oil producers; watch margins in upcoming results.

Airlines and truckers gain when fuel falls; energy producers lose.

items.headline: 2027 standard deduction rises to $33,200 for couples; 65+ extra goes to $2,100
items.caption: The standard deduction climbs $1,000 for married couples and $500 for singles in 2027. Older filers get a slightly bigger extra amount.
detail: Inflation adjustments lift the 2027 standard deduction to $33,200 for married couples filing jointly, $16,600 for singles and $24,950 for heads of household. These apply to returns filed in 2028.

People 65 and older get an extra amount on top: $2,100 for single or head-of-household filers and $1,700 per qualifying spouse for married filers. Blind filers get double. The separate $6,000 senior deduction still runs through 2028 and phases out above $75,000 of income for singles and $150,000 for couples.
money: Most people take the standard deduction; a higher one quietly lowers taxable income without extra work.
If your itemized deductions are close to the new amounts, 'bunching' gifts or payments into one year may help.
Seniors can stack the age-based extra with the $6,000 senior deduction if income qualifies.
risk: The $6,000 senior deduction phases out at higher incomes.

detail: The IRS Office of Professional Responsibility, which oversees tax practitioner conduct, has fewer than five AI-related cases among about 200. Director Thomas Curtin says such referrals are starting to tick up.
The office issued an alert in June applying its practitioner rules, called Circular 230, to AI use. Curtin said more guidance is coming in the next couple of months. The office has just 15 staff.
money: Ask your preparer how they use AI and who reviews the final return; you're responsible for what's filed.
Double-check AI-generated tax advice against IRS publications before acting on it.
A credentialed preparer (CPA, EA or attorney) is bound by IRS conduct rules, which gives you recourse.
risk: Errors on your return can bring penalties even if a tool made them.

items.headline: Judge bars ICE from reading an immigration lawyer's seized phone data for now
items.caption: A federal judge in Boston found the lawyer is likely to prove his phone was seized in retaliation for his speech. The government says it was part of an investigation.

visual.title: Lattarulo v. government
items: Phone seized at Boston Logan without a warrant
Data copied; phone returned 8 days later
Data must stay unreadable while the case goes on
Government cites a probe of his firm's hiring

detail: US District Judge Allison Burroughs granted a preliminary injunction for Andrew Lattarulo, part owner of an immigration law firm. Agents took his phone at Boston Logan Airport in September as he returned from Aruba, copied its data and returned it eight days later. He runs a popular Instagram account with know-your-rights videos.

The judge found he would likely show the search was retaliation for protected speech, and ordered the data kept unreadable until the case ends. She did not order it destroyed or rule on the Fourth Amendment. The government denies targeting his speech and says the search was tied to an inquiry into whether his firm employed unauthorized workers.
money: Border searches of phones are legal in many cases; travelers can limit what's stored on devices they carry.
Businesses should keep work-authorization (I-9) records complete, since hiring probes can be costly.
Legal fights like this can raise costs for small law firms; budgeting for compliance helps.
risk: This is an early ruling; the case continues.

items.headline: Texas bill would send $1,500 relief checks to every adult, paid from the rainy day fund
items.caption: State Sen. Roland Gutierrez filed SB 297, a $17 billion plan for one-time checks. It faces likely opposition in the Republican-led Senate.

visual.title: Texas SB 297
visual.label: One-time check proposed for adult Texans.

detail: Democratic State Sen. Roland Gutierrez of San Antonio filed Senate Bill 297. It would send $1,500 emergency relief checks to Texans 18 and older who lived in the state as of Jan. 1, 2027. People would apply online or by mail, and most checks would go out by the end of 2027.

The $17 billion cost would come from the state's roughly $27 billion rainy day fund, which needs legislative approval to tap. The bill argues an affordability crisis counts as a public calamity, the exception that allows direct payments. Democrats now control the Texas House, but the Republican Senate is likely to resist.
money: Nothing is approved; don't budget around a check that may never come.
If it passes, applications would run through 2028, so watch for the official comptroller process.
Beware scams promising early access to 'relief checks'; states never charge to apply.
risk: The bill faces long odds in the state Senate.

items.headline: Court lets DRAM price-fixing suit against Samsung, SK hynix and Micron move ahead

detail: A federal court let an antitrust lawsuit against Samsung, SK hynix and Micron proceed, denying their motions to dismiss, according to a Monday market report. The suit accuses them of conspiring to limit DRAM memory supply and raise prices.

Plaintiffs argue smaller makers cut supply first and the market leader followed about two months later. They say the restraint lasted over three years through a 697% price increase. The companies have sought to have the claims thrown out.
money: Memory prices feed into the cost of phones, PCs and servers, so a win for buyers could ease prices over time.
Legal risk adds to an already rough stretch for memory stocks; diversify rather than bet on one chipmaker.
Class actions take years; any payout to consumers is usually small and slow.
risk: The companies deny wrongdoing; the case is far from decided.

items.headline: Tyson edges past estimates and lifts its dividend 2%, but sees 2027 sales falling
items.caption: What's new: Tyson's numbers are out. Adjusted EPS of $0.61 edged past forecasts, beef lost $1.22B for the year, and 2027 sales are guided down 3.5% to 5.5%.
detail: Tyson Foods reported fiscal fourth-quarter sales of $14.59 billion, up about 5% from a year ago and roughly $490 million above estimates. Adjusted earnings were $0.61 a share, one cent better than forecasts but down 47% from last year. Without an extra week and legal accruals, sales would have fallen 4%.

Beef remains the problem. The segment lost about $1.22 billion for the year as volumes fell and cattle costs jumped. Chicken earned about $1.75 billion and prepared foods about $1.33 billion. For 2027, Tyson guides beef between a $300 million loss and $100 million of profit, as cattle supplies are expected to improve.
The company raised its yearly dividend by 2% and expects $1.7 billion to $2.15 billion in adjusted operating income in 2027. Shares rose in premarket trading.
money: A dividend payout ratio above 100% means profits don't fully cover the dividend yet; check that before buying for income.
High beef costs are hitting producers too; at the store, chicken and pork are often the cheaper protein.
Food stocks often get bought as a defensive move when tech swings; size any position with that in mind.
risk: Tyson expects lower sales in 2027, and beef could stay in the red.

Advantage produced about 87,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in the third quarter, mostly natural gas. Canadian Natural will also cover Advantage's 5% convertible debentures.
Advantage shareholders vote in January 2027. The deal also needs Canadian competition and Alberta court approval, with closing expected in the first quarter of 2027.

Energy buyers paying cash for gas reserves signals they expect demand to hold up; gas-heavy funds may benefit.
If you own the target, compare the deal price with the market price to see how sure traders think the deal is.

MTN shares fell 2.3%, cutting nearly R10 billion from its market value. Reports say MTN is weighing a cash offer with an option to take MTN shares. Both firms said talks are early and no deal is certain.

items.headline: Blackstone REIT buys 75% of 13 AWS data centers for ~$5B; Amazon leases them back
items.caption: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust is buying into two AWS campuses at a 7% starting yield. Amazon keeps 25% and signs leases of up to 32 years.
detail: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust, which trades as BXDC, agreed to buy a 75% stake in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services. They own 13 newly built data center shells across two AWS campuses. AWS keeps the other 25%.

AWS leases back 100% of the space on triple-net terms, meaning the tenant pays taxes, insurance and upkeep. The first lease term is 12 years and can stretch to 32 years. The price of about $5 billion works out to a 7.0% initial cap rate.
The company said the deal puts its IPO money to work. It expects to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.
money: A 7% cap rate means about $7 of yearly rent income per $100 paid; compare that with a 5.15% 10-year Treasury yield.
Data center REITs let regular investors own AI buildings for income; look at the tenant and lease length first.
Sale-leasebacks free up cash for Big Tech; watch whether more AI giants sell buildings to fund chips.
risk: If AI demand cools, data center values could fall even with long leases.
REIT prices often drop when interest rates rise.

items.headline: FAA outage traced to a router chain reaction; Duffy now wants $50B for air traffic control
items.caption: What's new: investigators say an Arkansas router swap set off a Texas router that flooded the network. Flights were mostly back Monday, with 284 cancellations by 7 a.m. ET.
detail: Investigators are looking at network gear at FAA sites in El Dorado, Arkansas, and Amarillo, Texas. Replacing a router in Arkansas reportedly triggered a newly replaced router in Texas to send out too much data, which overwhelmed routers at other control centers. The FAA turned off that broadcast feature on about 60 more routers.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said there is no sign of a cyberattack. He raised his request to modernize air traffic control to $50 billion, up from $30 billion. Congress approved $12.5 billion last year. Contractor L3Harris worked on the upgrades.
As of 7 a.m. ET Monday, FlightAware showed 284 canceled and 954 delayed U.S. flights. Since Friday, more than 18,500 flights were canceled.
money: If your flight was canceled, U.S. rules generally entitle you to a cash refund if you decline rebooking; ask for it.
Before Thanksgiving, book nonstop flights where you can; fewer connections means fewer chances to get stranded.
Credit cards with trip-delay coverage can repay hotel and meal costs; check your card's benefits page.
risk: The exact cause isn't confirmed, so more outages are possible during the busy holiday travel season.

items.headline: Democrats' 100-day plan: undo Medicaid cuts, extend ACA credits, restore SNAP. Who pays?
items.caption: Jeffries wants to reverse Medicaid cuts and extend ACA tax credits early next year. Proposed taxes on millionaires and buybacks would cover ACA credits, but not the Medicaid reversal.
detail: After winning the midterms, House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries is calling for reversing Medicaid cuts within the first 100 days, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits and restoring SNAP funding. The CBO estimates the Republican law trims federal Medicaid spending by about $1.2 trillion through 2035, with about 13 million fewer people covered.

Making the larger ACA credits permanent would add about $350 billion to deficits over 10 years and help about 3.8 million more people get insurance, per the CBO. Other ideas include adding dental, vision and hearing to Medicare.

Proposed pay-fors include a surtax on incomes over $1 million, about $264 billion, and raising the stock buyback tax from 1% to 4%, about $242 billion to $300 billion. Critics, including the Cato Institute, doubt the plan adds up, and Trump could veto it.
money: If you buy ACA coverage, enroll by Dec. 15 at today's prices; don't count on a subsidy fix arriving in time.
On Medicaid or SNAP? Keep your income and work records current so you don't lose benefits on paperwork.
A buyback tax hike could nudge companies toward dividends; income investors may want to watch.
risk: None of this is law; a Trump veto or Senate math could block it.
Plans could change a lot before the new Congress starts.

items.headline: Iran says it sent drones at a US-used base in Bahrain; Bahrain says it shot them down
items.caption: Bahrain issued its first nationwide alerts since September. Oil stayed calm, with Brent near $94 to $96 as Hormuz traffic recovers.

items.t: IRGC: six drones aimed at Al Rifaa base radar
Saudi Arabia downs Houthi missiles near Riyadh

detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it launched six drones at US air defense radar at the Al Rifaa helicopter base in Bahrain. It called the attack payback for US actions. Bahrain's military said it intercepted and destroyed several Iranian attacks. No damage or injuries were reported, and the US did not confirm a hit.

It was Bahrain's first nationwide alert since September and Iran's first strike on a Gulf state in weeks. Bahrain hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. Saudi Arabia also said it intercepted two Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh.
Oil barely reacted. Brent hovered between about $94 and $96 Monday as Hormuz shipping nears prewar levels and the IEA says supply now tops demand.
money: Oil has held steady despite new attacks; gas prices could keep easing if supply stays strong.
Energy stocks can drop when oil glut fears grow; check how much of your portfolio sits in energy.

items.headline: Medicaid work rules still start Jan. 1, but states can't cut people off until July 1
items.caption: Federal officials gave states six more months before removing anyone for not meeting the new work rule. States can still act early.
detail: The federal Medicaid agency told states Friday that the new work requirement still takes effect nationwide on Jan. 1. But states can now wait until July 1 to deny or end coverage for people who don't comply. States may still start earlier.

The rule covers adults in the Medicaid expansion adopted by 40 states, mostly lower-income adults without kids at home. Many must work, volunteer or study at least 80 hours a month. People over 64, caregivers of children under 14 and the medically frail are exempt.
States asked for time to build staff and systems. In Nebraska, which started early, 533 people were denied, mostly over paperwork.
money: If you're on Medicaid, start keeping pay stubs or volunteer logs now so you're ready to report hours.
Check if you qualify for an exemption, such as caring for a child under 14.

risk: Your state may still enforce early, so check your state's own dates.

items.headline: IRS reminder: no itemizing needed to deduct up to $1,000 in charity gifts for 2026

detail: The IRS is reminding taxpayers that a permanent charity deduction for people who don't itemize begins with tax year 2026. Singles can deduct up to $1,000 of cash gifts, and married couples filing jointly up to $2,000.

items.headline: Hackers hijack about 64,000 bitcoin mining machines but fail to mine a single block

detail: Starting around 8 p.m. Central time on Nov. 14, attackers took over roughly 64,000 bitcoin mining machines. They redirected about 13 EH/s of hashpower to the OCEAN pool and set the payout to an address they controlled.
Hosting firm CoreX raised the alarm. OCEAN's hashrate briefly neared 50 EH/s. CoreX later said the hijacked power fell to about 100 PH/s and the attack appeared to end Nov. 15.
The attackers mined no blocks. But affected miners lost the revenue they would have earned. One operator blamed Luxor's Commander management software, which has not been confirmed.
money: If you own mining stocks, ask how they secure their fleet software. Lost hashing time is lost revenue.
Self-hosting a miner? Change default passwords and lock down remote management tools.
Security incidents keep piling up in crypto. Keep crypto a small part of your money.

detail: Google DeepMind said its new AlphaProof Code system formally verified several core security guarantees of the Signal messaging protocol. The proof of concept took about four weeks, with a head start from earlier verification work.

Limits are real. It didn't cover the full mobile app, Google didn't share the cost, and researchers say scaling it up has a long way to go.

Changes in district funding can affect local property tax debates. Watch your school board's budget hearings.

District budgets could face cuts if funding shifts.

items.headline: Ballot results that change state taxes in 2027, from Florida to Washington
items.caption: Florida raised its homestead break, North Carolina cut its income tax cap, and Washington kept its millionaire tax. Some results are still unofficial.

rows.s: 2/3 vote to raise income tax rates

detail: Florida voters raised the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, and cut the cap on yearly assessment increases for non-homestead property from 10% to 5%.

North Carolina voters appear to have lowered the state income tax rate cap from 7% to 3.5%. Iowa now needs a two-thirds legislative vote to raise income tax rates. Colorado's Amendment 87, creating graduated rates up to 8.4% on income over $1 million, appears to have narrowly passed.

California's Prop 3 appears to make its high-earner rates of 10.3% to 12.3% permanent, while the billionaire wealth tax failed. In Washington, 58% rejected repealing the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million.
money: Florida homeowners: check that your homestead exemption is filed. The bigger break only helps if it's on record.
Colorado high earners may want to review 2027 withholding and timing of big income like bonuses or stock sales.
Moving for taxes? Compare total costs, including property and sales taxes, not just income tax rates.
risk: Results are unofficial until certified.
Lawsuits or new laws can change how measures take effect.

detail: JPMorgan Chase filed a new state layoff notice for 91 jobs in Jersey City, effective between Oct. 30 and Jan. 24, 2027. It's the bank's sixth New Jersey notice this year, for 632 roles in that state.

Notices in New Jersey, Texas and California cover at least 929 positions in 2026. That includes 244 roles at its Plano, Texas campus, most of them fraud specialist jobs. TheStreet notes this is not a confirmed total of finished layoffs.
The bank is still growing. It had 322,964 employees on Sept. 30, up 4,811 from a year earlier. Across finance, announced job cuts are about half of last year's pace, per Challenger, Gray & Christmas.
money: Big companies often cut some teams while hiring in others. If you work in banking, watch which roles are shrinking, like fraud review, and which are growing.
State WARN notice lists are public. Checking them can give you early warning about layoffs at your employer.
Even when headcount grows, a steady emergency fund protects you if your own team gets cut.
risk: More rounds could follow; JPMorgan has filed notices roughly every month or two this year.
AI was cited in about 20% of all announced US job cuts this year, per Challenger.

Bloomberg reported this month that Disney is moving toward thousands of job cuts, with some managers asked to find 20% in yearly savings. Deadline says a round could land in early 2027. Disney declined to comment.

Options traders are pricing a 6.3% move either way. Disney's last eight reports moved the stock 6.1% on average. The board usually sets the year's dividend with this report; last year it raised it 50% to $1.50.

Dividend investors: watch for the new yearly dividend, which is usually set with this report.
If you're a Disney+ or parks customer, cost cuts can come with price or perk changes. Watch for deals around the holidays.
risk: The stock sits near its 52-week high, so a miss could hit harder.
Job-cut numbers and timing are unconfirmed reports, not company announcements.

items.headline: Tyson reports today: chicken profits soar while beef losses pile up

visual.title: Tyson Q4 expectations

detail: Tyson Foods reports fiscal fourth-quarter results Monday before the market opens. Consensus calls for 65 cents a share, down from $1.15, on about $13.88 billion in sales, per Earnings Whispers.

Beef is the problem. Tyson lost $138 million in beef last quarter as volume fell nearly 16%, and it widened its full-year beef loss forecast to $500 million to $650 million. It has closed several beef plants as cattle supplies hit multi-decade lows.

Chicken is the bright spot. That unit earned $488 million last quarter, and Tyson raised its full-year chicken outlook to $1.9 billion to $2.05 billion. Investors also want a first look at fiscal 2027 plans.
money: Tight cattle supply has kept beef prices high. Chicken and pork can stretch a grocery budget, especially before holiday meals.
If you own Tyson, the 2027 outlook may move the stock more than this quarter's numbers.
Food stocks with mixed units show why diversification matters: one strong segment can offset a weak one.
risk: Beef losses could widen further if cattle herds stay small.
Chicken faces a tough comparison with a record quarter a year ago.

items.headline: Cruise giant MSC nears a deal for 80% of rescued German shipyard Meyer Werft
items.caption: Der Spiegel says MSC could sign as soon as Tuesday for most of the yard. Germany's government and Lower Saxony bailed it out in 2024.

items.st: Signing reported for Nov 17; state says not this week

detail: MSC Group of Geneva is close to a deal for about 80% of Meyer Werft, the German shipyard that builds cruise ships. Der Spiegel reported a signing could come Tuesday, Nov. 17. Lower Saxony said it doesn't plan to sign any sale contracts in the coming week.

The federal government and Lower Saxony each own about 40% after a 2024 rescue that put in €400 million of equity and a €2.6 billion state-backed credit line. The Meyer family holds about 20% and wants to stay on.

The yard's 2025 revenue was €2.83 billion, but it lost €383.8 million. A reported order for four new ships could be worth up to €10 billion through 2033. The price MSC would pay hasn't been disclosed.
money: New ship orders point to strong cruise demand. If you cruise, booking early often locks in better cabin prices.
Cruise stocks like Royal Caribbean, Carnival and Norwegian can move on shipbuilding news. Know what you own in travel funds.
Government rescues can end with a sale. Watch whether taxpayers get their money back, a sign of how bailouts work.
risk: The deal date is unconfirmed, and the state denies signing this week.
The yard is still losing money and restructuring through 2028.

items.headline: California blocks insurers from dropping 50,000 homes near the Dove Fire for a year
items.caption: Commissioner Lara ordered a one-year ban on cancellations and nonrenewals in parts of three counties. Insurers must offer to undo notices already sent.

visual.title: Dove Fire insurance moratorium

detail: California Insurance Commissioner Ricardo Lara issued a one-year moratorium on cancellations and nonrenewals for about 50,000 homeowners in Tuolumne, Stanislaus and Calaveras counties. It follows Gov. Newsom's Oct. 15 emergency declaration for the Dove Fire.
It covers 15 ZIP codes in or near the fire area, whether or not a home was damaged. It also reaches some commercial policies, such as HOAs, apartment complexes, condo associations and senior living.

Insurers that sent wildfire-related cancellation or nonrenewal notices on or after Oct. 15 must offer to rescind them. The state says such moratoriums protected more than 1.2 million homeowners in 2025.
money: If you live in these counties and got a nonrenewal notice after Oct. 15, contact your insurer and ask for reinstatement.
The moratorium blocks dropping you, not rate hikes. Shop rates and ask about wildfire mitigation discounts.
Take photos of your home and belongings now. A home inventory speeds up any future claim.
risk: After one year, insurers can drop policies again unless the ban is extended.
The moratorium does not cap premiums.

AMD says its top EPYC 9996 chip delivers up to 3.7 times the performance of an Nvidia Vera CPU system and 2.2 times an Intel Xeon 6980P system. These are AMD's own test claims. The top chips pack 256 cores on TSMC's 2-nanometer process.
Meta is the lead customer. AMD argues AI agents need far more regular CPUs alongside AI accelerators, a bet that could widen its market as AI spending grows.

Company benchmark claims are marketing until independent tests confirm them. Don't buy a stock on a press release.
Cheaper, faster servers can lower cloud costs over time, which could eventually show up in prices for AI tools.
risk: Cloud availability is still pending, so real sales may take quarters to show.
Chip stocks have been very volatile this month.

items.headline: Crypto market bill looks stuck for 2026; SEC nominees face senators Thursday
items.caption: The CLARITY Act fell 11 votes short in September and seems unlikely to move in the lame duck. Senate Banking holds a hearing on two SEC picks Nov. 19.

items.t: Trump names 2 SEC and 2 CFTC picks

detail: The CLARITY Act, a bill to set rules for crypto markets, is unlikely to advance before the new Congress, crypto.news reports. A September 15 Senate vote to end debate failed 49–50, 11 short of the 60 needed. The House passed it 294–134 in July 2025.

Congress is focused on nominees instead. On Nov. 12, Trump nominated Steven Levine and Kristin Johnson to the SEC and Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland to the CFTC. Senate Banking holds a hearing on the SEC picks Nov. 19. The CFTC now has only one sitting commissioner.
Stablecoin rules are moving separately. The OCC's final rule for payment stablecoin issuers, under the 2025 GENIUS Act, takes effect Jan. 18, 2027.
money: Without a market-structure law, crypto rules stay murky. That uncertainty is one reason prices swing so hard; size crypto bets accordingly.
Stablecoin rules on reserves and redemptions take effect in January. Favor stablecoins from issuers that publish regular reserve audits.
Keep records of every crypto trade. Whatever rules come, the IRS already taxes crypto gains.
risk: Democrats take control in January, which could reshape any crypto bill.
Confirmation votes may slip into 2027.

items.headline: US plans to deport about 150 Afghans via Pakistan; flight reset for Nov. 16
items.caption: An advocacy group says the flight was rescheduled to today. A court order shields only five people, and Democrats are pushing a bill to restore Afghans' protected status.

visual.title: The Afghan deportation fight
items: About 150 Afghans slated for removal via Pakistan
Flight reportedly moved to Nov. 16; DHS won't confirm
About 11,700 Afghans had TPS before it was revoked in 2025
Discharge petition needs 218; Democrats hold 214 seats

detail: The US plans to deport about 150 Afghans to Afghanistan by way of Pakistan, with media reports saying the flight would leave from Louisiana. Shawn VanDiver of AfghanEvac said it was rescheduled to Nov. 16. DHS declined to confirm.

A judge's order, first issued Nov. 3 and extended indefinitely Nov. 7, protects only five people represented by one legal group. US officials ended Temporary Protected Status for Afghans in May 2025; DHS had estimated about 11,700 held it.

Rep. Jason Crow's Afghanistan TPS Act would restore that status. A discharge petition needs 218 signatures, so at least four Republicans would have to join. Democrats take the House majority in January. Supporters of the removals say people without legal status should leave; opponents cite safety risks under Taliban rule.
money: Immigration cases can be costly. Many nonprofits offer free or low-cost legal help; check before paying a private lawyer.
Families facing removal should keep copies of key financial papers and give a trusted person access to bank accounts.
Employers with immigrant staff should plan for sudden departures that could affect payroll and operations.
risk: Timing could change again with court rulings or DHS decisions.
Whether the president would sign a TPS bill is unclear.

Medicaid gets the largest increase at $150 million, including help for people on a disability-services waitlist. Education gets $90 million, with $70 million for Education Freedom Accounts used by more than 50,000 students. SNAP administration gets $25 million.

Sanders said the plan holds down government growth to leave room for tax cuts, but no dollar figure was given. Possible one-time surplus spending includes $200 million for Medicaid and $50 million for the state's possible share of SNAP benefits.
money: Arkansans: watch for income tax cut details in the coming session. A lower rate could change your 2027 withholding.
Families using Education Freedom Accounts may see more funding; check eligibility and deadlines.
The $50 million SNAP set-aside reflects new federal rules shifting food aid costs to states, a trend to watch in every state.
risk: Tax cut size and timing are not yet set.
Federal Medicaid and SNAP changes could strain the budget.

items.headline: Japan's economy unexpectedly shrinks in Q3 as shoppers pull back
items.caption: Japan's GDP fell 0.1% at an annual pace in July to September, when economists expected growth. It's the first drop in four quarters.

visual.title: Japan Q3 GDP, annualized
visual.foot: Reuters: prior quarter revised to 1.7% growth

detail: Japan's economy contracted 0.1% at an annualized rate in the third quarter. A Reuters poll had expected 0.3% growth. Quarter over quarter, output was basically flat.

Consumer spending, more than half the economy, fell 0.3%. Rain, typhoons, high prices and a payback after earlier car and air-conditioner buying all hurt. Business investment rose 1.6%, helped by AI and labor-saving projects. Higher energy imports took 0.6 points off growth.
The Bank of Japan has raised rates twice this year, in June and September. Its rate is 1.25%, and a move to 1.5% in December is widely expected. The dollar is pressing toward 160 yen.
money: A weak yen makes Japan trips cheaper for Americans. Watch fares and hotel deals if you plan travel.
If you own international stock funds, Japan is often one of the biggest country weights. Check your fund's mix.
Business investment in AI is still growing even as shoppers pull back, a theme showing up across many economies.
risk: Weak growth could make the BOJ delay its December hike, which could push the yen even lower.
A revised GDP estimate comes next month and could change the picture.

Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs told the Wall Street Journal it did not investigate Huang. That disputes an earlier report that local authorities had probed her.

If you own chip funds, Nvidia is often the largest holding. Know how much of your money rides on one name.
